Latest Update: Jensen Huang: Spy row, affairs leave Nvidia without its rockstar CEO

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1078 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia's board met late Wednesday to decide on CEO Jensen Huang's future as reports emerged of other extramarital affairs — this time with employees.
  • In a statement issued on Thursday, the world's most valuable chip supplier noted Huang was resigning as President, CEO and board member, effective immediately.
  • The firm added that current Vice President and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Colette Kress would become interim CEO.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia's board met late Wednesday to decide on CEO Jensen Huang's future as reports emerged of other extramarital affairs — this time with employees.

In a statement issued on Thursday, the world's most valuable chip supplier noted Huang was resigning as President, CEO and board member, effective immediately.

The firm added that current Vice President and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Colette Kress would become interim CEO.

Under Nvidia's bylaws, Huang can be removed "with or without cause" by a majority vote of its 11 directors.

The New York Times first reported that the 63-year-old Huang had an affair with a senior Nvidia executive who reported directly to him.

Later Thursday, Reuters news agency alleged an intimate relationship between Huang and a second employee, citing unidentified sources.

Those revelations emerged just three days after Huang admitted a relationship with a Chinese woman, whom United States intelligence agencies believe was spying for China. The woman, Alice Huang — no relation — is a former executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud computing firm that runs artificial intelligence (AI) data centers across Southeast Asia and is a major client of Nvidia.

The US government is investigating the startup on suspicion that it secretly sent some of its Nvidia chips to China, violating Washington's curbs on high-end semiconductors.

Those advanced Nvidia processors ‌are ​used to train and run the large AI models behind chatbots and other generative AI products.

Recent findings suggest that megaspeed denies the allegations and on Thursday pledged to cooperate with US investigators. Huang, the alleged spy, has been barred from entering Singapore and Taiwan — a key chipmaking island.

While Nvidia's board backed its CEO after the first scandal emerged, market watchers believe the second caused too much reputational damage to one of the world's top three companies by market value.

According to The Wall Street Journal, Huang doesn't believe in formal succession planning, so with little notice, Nvidia appointed CFO Kress as interim CEO.

Bloomberg reported Wednesday that Nvidia’s board is working with advisers to identify potential permanent successors.

Sources indicate that kress, other senior Nvidia executives and members of Huang's own family have been mooted as replacements. The family members include his daughter Madison, a senior director of product marketing, and his son Spencer, who currently works in the firm's robotics division.

Rumors also abound over a longer-term solution. On India's CNBC-TV18, Jeffrey Sonnenfeld from the Yale School of Management floated former Apple CEO Tim Cook and ex-Google CEO Eric Schmidt.

US President Donald Trump also backed Cook on social media, writing: "A Legend replaces a Legend.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The scandals have certainly hit Nvidia's market value. Since the first extramarital affair emerged on Sunday, the chipmaker's market capitalization has fallen by well over $600 billion to $4.2 trillion.

In a recent development, nvidia shares were down more than 9% in premarket trading Thursday, after dropping by 10% earlier this week. Some analysts expect the stock price to struggle in the short term.

Nvidia stock hit all-time highs just a month ago as US technology giants continued to announce billions in spending on AI infrastructure.

Demand for Nvidia's advanced chips is so high, however, that many market analysts expect little impact on near-term sales.

"While Jensen [Huang] is the heart and lungs of the Nvidia story…the company and its leading-edge GPU technology will go on and [his departure] does not change the entrenched position Nvidia has in the AI Revolution chip arms race," mentioned Dan Ives, a partner, senior managing director and tech analyst at Yorkville Ives, a US-based merchant bank.

Analysts see the biggest long-term risk in strategy and execution. After all, Huang was the leader who picked which ideas Nvidia should bet heavily on and got the whole company behind them.

His sudden exit is also seen as highly disruptive to the chip designer's strong relationships with AI hyperscalers, Taiwanese chip producer TSMC and foreign governments — especially China.

Huang was Nvidia's main lobbyist on US chip export rules and persuaded US President Donald Trump to ease some curbs on China last year.

Huang is often called a rockstar CEO for his leather jackets instead of suits.

Like Elon Musk of Tesla and SpaceX, he was also seen as a key-person risk as Nvidia’s public image, strategic direction and technical decisions became closely tied to him.

Huang steered the company for more than three decades and was also respected for his hands-on involvement in product architecture and engineering decisions.

He also insisted on a flat management structure, with around 60 executives reporting directly to him.

Huang has run the manufacturer so tightly around his own technical judgment and product decisions that investors may have little sense of how it would function without him.

At the same time, Nvidia is no longer the startup Huang founded in 1993. The company has built deep expertise in chip design and software, creating a durable moat that helps protect its huge profits, which topped $120.1 billion last year.

Some analysts argue that its central role in the AI hardware buildout makes it less dependent on Huang’s day-to-day input.

China is rapidly playing catch-up with the US in the global race for AI dominance.

While Chinese AI models have lagged behind the likes of ChatGPT and Claude, recent updates from DeepSeek, Alibaba and Moonshot have closed much of the gap on benchmark tests and often beat US rivals on cost and speed.

Beijing is also investing heavily in domestic chips and data centers to reduce reliance on US hardware.

The US has curbed exports to China of Nvidia's most advanced AI chips.

However, this move has only slowed the pace of China's AI ambitions.

Reuters reported Thursday that Chinese AI firms are now trying to rent Nvidia-powered computing capacity at data centers outside China, amid fears the US could further tighten restrictions on advanced chips.

Also Thursday, Beijing accused the US of using the Nvidia spying claims as a pretext to impose a technological "blockade" on China.

The concern is likely to dominate talks next week between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at the APEC gathering in Shenzhen in southern China.

Saliba has fight on his hands to usurp ‘unbelievable’ Konsa

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that from the moment Ezri Konsa pulled on an Arsenal shirt, he has moved with all the composure of a man who knows exactly where to be and when.
  • The loss of Saliba to a long-term back injury was supposed to be a major problem for Arsenal.
  • “Unbelievable,” Mikel Arteta, the Arsenal manager, said of his £55m signing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that from the moment Ezri Konsa pulled on an Arsenal shirt, he has moved with all the composure of a man who knows exactly where to be and when. The centre-back has required no adaptation period in north London, where he has filled the considerable shoes of William Saliba with such class that Arsenal have hardly missed the Frenchman at all.

The loss of Saliba to a long-term back injury was supposed to be a major problem for Arsenal. Instead, the situation has now reached a point where some fans are wondering how Saliba will get back into the side. That may prove a little extreme, but the fact there is even a discussion is proof of Konsa’s superb impact at the Emirates Stadium.

“Unbelievable,” Mikel Arteta, the Arsenal manager, said of his £55m signing. “He’s come to a huge club and to position yourself in that manner, and to perform at the level he is, it is very difficult to do. We are really lucky to have him.”.

In Arsenal’s latest victory, their seventh from eight matches in the Premier League this season, Konsa offered all of his usual defensive security and calmness in possession. Even more excitingly, he also scored his first goal for the club, smashed in from close range after a corner had caused chaos in Everton’s penalty area. It was Arsenal’s first set-piece goal of the season.

“I have been waiting to score my first goal for a while,” Konsa stated. “I spoke to the set-piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well. We felt as players that it was coming, and today was the day.”.

Industry observers note that some eyebrows were raised when Arsenal paid such a large fee to sign Konsa from Aston Villa. The Villa fans, though, were not among those who questioned the price or the player’s ability. They have known for years at Villa Park that Konsa is a player of the highest quality, and they will not be surprised by his exceptional start to his Arsenal career.

In a recent development, the same is true of the Arsenal players. Arteta asked the England internationals in his squad about Konsa before buying him, and the feedback was overwhelmingly positive. Konsa was already close friends with Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze before completing his transfer from Villa.

In a recent development, konsa’s start to life at Arsenal is all the more impressive because he did not even have a pre-season. He effectively came straight from the World Cup into the club, and has been starting games since early September. His first start was against Chelsea, when he endeared himself to the home fans with a crunching tackle on former team-mate Morgan Rogers.

Sources indicate that konsa, 29, has rapidly built a strong relationship with Gabriel Magalhães, his defensive partner who scored Arsenal’s other goal here against Everton, from Ben White’s cross. For both centre-backs to find the net felt like a throwback to last year, when Arsenal were so dangerous from crosses, and underlined how Arteta’s team are capable of hurting their opponents in many different ways.

It has been revealed that the nature of the goals might give a misleading impression of Arsenal’s performance, though. This was not a gritty win. Arteta’s side produced some excellent passing moves and circulated the ball with menace throughout the game. They were also a little open at times, especially in the first half when Everton created a handful of decent chances.

Thierno Barry missed the best of those opportunities, with the score at 1-0. It was the closest the visitors came to hurting the champions, aside from some of James Tarkowski’s full-blooded tackles. “I felt we didn’t really get to a level that was good enough to get near them,” admitted David Moyes, the Everton manager.

It has been revealed that the victory, combined with Manchester City’s defeat earlier in the day, put Arsenal level on points at the top of the table. Aside from the extraordinary thrashing at Brighton, Arteta’s side have looked just as solid, if not more so, than last season. That speaks volumes of the quality in the team, of course, but also says plenty about the way Konsa has adjusted to his newly introduced surroundings. Thanks to him, Saliba’s absence has not hurt at all.

It has been revealed that “Great feeling, it always is. A clean sheet, a goal – my first goal for the club – so a fantastic day overall.

In a recent development, “I’ve been waiting to score my first goal for a while. I spoke to the set piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well, so it was only right that I got the goal today.

“I’ve come to this stadium for many seasons, I know how tough it is to play against us. It’s not surprising to me.

Recent findings suggest that “We are champions and to be champions you’ve got to win games consistently. This is our home and we want to win as many games here as possible.”.

All over at the Emirates and the champions go level on points with Manchester City at the top of the table.

It has been revealed that they kept another clean sheet and scored from a set-piece again. All is right in Arsenal’s world!

Oscar Bobb’s first Premier League goal for Fulham earned a 1-0 win over Coventry that lifted the Cottagers clear of the relegation zone.

Bobb produced a fine bit of individual skill to strike in the 80th minute as he twisted his way into the box and bent a shot into the far corner, only his second goal for the club in any competition since his £27million move from Manchester City back in January.

That was enough to give Fulham their first away win in nine attempts, a run that dated back to February, only a week after they ended their winless start to the league campaign by edging out Hull 1-0 as the pressure continues to ease on Alvaro Arbeloa.

Josh King had earlier hit the post for the visitors, who edged Coventry in just about every department to leave Frank Lampard’s side second-bottom of the table.

The hosts had only brief spells of sustained possession in Fulham’s half, but did little to trouble Bernd Leno on a frustrating afternoon which bought the CBS Arena back down to earth after their 4-1 win over Newcastle in their last home outing.

Odegaard drives a shot high over the ball as Arsenal close in on another clean sheet.

Probably sums up Zubimendi’s season so far that he finally gets some meaningful minutes in the Premier League and ends up getting smashed in the face and covered in his own blood. This is after he got injured in a cool-down a few weeks ago. When your luck’s out...

Eight minutes added on at the Emirates.

Brilliant play from Oscar Bobb as he cuts inside on his left foot and bends a shot into the far bottom corner for the away side.

EvertonOFF Dewsbury-HallON Alcaraz.

Treatment is needed for Zubimendi after he is caught on the nose by Barry.

It has been revealed that substantial chance for Everton. Garner whips a teasing cross into the box, Dewsbury-Hall meets it with his head on the run but the ball flies just wide of the post.

This game is not over for Arsenal yet.

ArsenalOFF Rice, EzeON Zubimendi, Dowman.

EvertonOFF Johnson, Mykolenko ON Dibling, Hackney.

Tarkowski is the latest yellow card for Everton after a foul on Havertz.

It has been revealed that eze with a poor cross into the box. He fails to run back swiftly and Arteta sprints to the edge of the touchline and goes berserk at the midfielder.

How have Arsenal reacted to their top scorer Saka being injured? Both of their centre backs have scored for the first time this season.

On his 200 Premier League appearance for Arsenal, Gabriel marks it with his first goal of the season.

It is a lovely move with slick one-touch passing. The ball is fed to White making a run down the outside and he clips the ball to the far post for Gabriel to head home.

OFF Merino, Lewis-Skelly, GyokeresON Calafiori, Guimaraes, Havertz.

Garner is booked for Everton now after barging into Merino off the ball.

Sources indicate that arteta is shown a yellow card for something. Not sure what for yet. But the Arsenal manager is looking to make some changes off the bench.

Sources indicate that arsenal have been guilty of overplaying today. Opting for the extra pass rather than taking a shot. The game is open at the moment and that makes things dangerous for the home side.

Yellow card for Lewis-Skelly after bringing down Johnson. Gabriel is back on the pitch and seems happy enough to continue.

Arsenal have defensive options in Timber, Hincapie, Calafiori and Mosquera if Arteta wants to avoid taking any risks.

A worry for Arsenal as Gabriel jars his knee into the ground as he tries to clear the ball. The Brazilian is receiving treatment and hobbles off the pitch.

Industry observers note that gabriel immediately raised his hand for medical attention after making that clearance. He really extended his leg to get the ball away. Looks to be in a lot of pain.

Latest corner from Arsenal after Eze’s shot is blocked by Rohl. Rice’s delivery into the near post is headed clear to Odegaard, who shoots ambitiously from distance and Pickford collects the ball comfortably.

In a recent development, arsenal get the match restarted. The longer the match goes on without extending the lead, Everton will think they have a chance.

Before today, Arsenal had averaged five corners per match in the Premier League this season. In the first 45 minutes here, they had 10 corners.

Yellow card for Mykolenko after he catches White wide on the right. Rice whips the ball in and Merino meets it with a flick goalwards but the ball goes over the bar.

That is the final touch of the half and the players are running off to get dry!

In a recent development, significant chance for Everton. White thinks he has time when he heads the ball back to Raya but he does not connect well and Barry is there to pick it up and he flicks a shot at goal but Raya reacts rapidly to parry the ball.

Raya is penalised for taking too long with the ball and Everton have a cheap corner. Danger is cleared by Arsenal as they force Everton back into their half.

According to recent reports, the conditions are terrible at the moment. Heavy wind and rain causing havoc.

A lot of set-pieces for Arsenal today as they continue to put Everton under the cosh. Can they take advantage of their dominance again before the break?

Arsenal have found their groove again, with Madueke twice going close to extending their lead. Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Odegaard and Merino are forming a box in midfield and Everton don’t seem to know how to shut them down.

Another effort at goal for Madueke. This one is a snapshot from the edge of the box that goes into the side netting.

In a recent development, madueke should do better. Rice finds him and the winger drives into the box. He takes a shot but drags a right-footed effort wide.

Chance for Arsenal. Rice finds space behind the Everton midfield and drives forward. He plays a pass to Lewis-Skelly, who lays it off to Eze. The England midfielder sidefoots a cross into the box but no one in an Arsenal shirt is there to meet it.

Courtesy of Opta: Arsenal scored their first set-piece goal in all competitions (not including penalties) since May of last season against Crystal Palace, ending a run of 13 games without one.

Industry observers note that george is looking lively for Everton. He tries to come inside and whip an effort to the far corner but the ball deflects wide.

From the corner, Gabriel clears off the line after Raya loses track of the ball.

Sources indicate that everton have responded impressively to the Konsa goal and have been the better team since falling behind. Midfielders Garner and Armstrong are growing into the game quite nicely.

According to recent reports, everton have responded well to going behind here. The early goal against them will have ripped up any intends to sit deep and play on the counter.

Set-pieces are back on the menu for Arsenal. Ezri Konsa’s first goal for the club is their first goal from a corner this season, which will come as a relief to set-piece coach Nicolas Jover. “Set piece again, ole ole,” sing the Arsenal fans. Arteta’s side had started the game on the front foot.

Industry observers note that arsenal had not scored from a corner this season... until now. Konsa breaks the deadlock after a melee in the box and his pokes the ball into the net.

A couple of early set pieces from Declan Rice. Everton do well to clear the danger. But have another one now...

Sources indicate that horrible conditions at the Emirates today. The rain has been lashing down. The Emirates drainage system is usually able to cope with this sort of thing. If the wind picks up, that’s likely to be a bigger problem for the two teams.

After a minute’s applause in honour of Ken Friar, the match makes a prompt start at the Emirates.

On bouncing back from defeat...

According to recent reports, “Yeah, we’ve had a good start. Obviously, we had a bit of a blip last week against Chelsea. I don’t think we, as a team, won first and second balls enough and that’s something the manager wants us to get back to today. You’ve got to win your battles.”.

On what makes Arsenal difficult to play...

Industry observers note that “They’re reigning Premier League champions, a top side that has been knocking on the door to win the title for a few years before as well. They’re a team at a high level but this is what Premier League football is all about and it’s up to us to get a result.”.

“Well, we play every two-and-a-half days so we didn’t have much time to recover, so we need full energy. There are certain specific players as well that they fit really well for the game that we expect today and that’s how we start.”.

“A very competitive team, a really well organised team. I think that it’s very clear what they want to do, where they want to take the game. The threats, when they have a space to run, any time that they are able to put the ball in their box, you know the presence and aggression that they have. So, yeah, we have to really be at it and be very aggressive from the beginning.”.

One of the clearest signs a football club is in a good place is when the debate switches from whether the team are winning to how they are winning.

Industry observers note that this is currently Arsenal and Mikel Arteta’s world. For years, Arsenal coaches and players were asked how and when they would start collecting major trophies again. With no concern about their capacity to challenge for top honours over the coming years, the style has become the main focus.

It’s a welcome “problem” – or some might argue a non-existent one – for Arteta while his side is so strong. Building a fortress is the expensive, time-consuming and difficult part. Once it’s constructed and established, how you decorate it is a matter of taste.

Whether neutrals will hold the current champions in the same regard as the great Arsène Wenger sides will be a trivial concern if Arteta does what no Arsenal manager has since 1935 – defend the league title – and then add a few more, which is a serious possibility based on the balance of power in England and the likely punishment heading Manchester City’s way.

Today there will be tributes to Ken Friar, who passed away at the age of 92 earlier this year. Advertising boards outside the Emirates Stadium have been taken over by images of Friar, who had a remarkable 70-year association with the club.

In today’s programme, captain Martin Odegaard has written the following: “It’s exceptional people like Ken Friar who have built the club into what it is today, and we as the current team are the ones privileged to continue his legacy.”.

This is a first Premier League start of the season for Viktor Gyokeres, who has been behind Kai Havertz in the pecking order over the past few months. Gyokeres has yet to score in nine appearances in all competitions this season, although he would (understandably) make the point that it’s harder to do so when you are coming off the bench late in games.

For Arsenal, Arteta shuffles his team after the draw against Bayern: White, Lewis-Skelly, Merino, Eze and Gyokeres start.

Max Dowman, who scored a memorable goal in this fixture last season, is on the bench.

For Everton, Jack Grealish misses today’s game due to sickness, while Jarrad Branthwaite is absent because of concussion protocols despite finishing last week’s match with Chelsea after a head collision with Emi Martinez.

Arsenal: Raya, White, Gabriel, Konsa, Lewis-Skelly, Rice, Merino, Odegaard, Madueke, Eze, Gyokeres.Subs: Arrizabalaga, Timber, Hincapie, Calafiori, Mosquera, Zubimendi, Guimaraes, Dowman, Havertz.

Everton: Pickford, Tarkowski, O’Brien, Armstrong, Rohl, Dewsbury-Hall, George, Barry, Garner, Mykolenko, JohnsonSubs: Travers, King, Maitland-Niles, Keane, Dibling, Norgaard, Alcaraz, Hackney, Braiden Graham.

Hello and welcome to coverage from the Emirates as Premier League champions Arsenal host Everton.

Mikel Arteta’s men produced a good performance in midweek to draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League while David Moyes’s squad have had the week off following their 2-0 defeat by Chelsea last weekend.

Arteta said: “We’re having three games in six days so we know what’s happening, especially when the games are so demanding and the necessity is to win. We know that, so we prepare the players for those scenarios and do the best we possibly can.

Sources indicate that “I know David so well and how he sets the team, the quality they have in their organisation and individually. It’s no coincidence they didn’t lose before their last game. They have a really good team, which we know because in recent clashes, it’s always been a really difficult game for us.”.

Both teams enter this game having been beaten just once this season but eight points separate them with Arsenal in second and Everton in eighth.

According to recent reports, moyes said: “It’s not an easy game and never has been over many years. We look forward to it; they had a game in midweek, and we have to try and capitalise on that. I thought we did really well last year against them; we played really well down at Arsenal, and I hope we can do the same.

“When I look back at the team we had out, we were pretty threadbare at that time, but we did a good job, and I hope we can do it again. Obviously Arsenal have some many different tools in their bag and people they can use in different positions, so we’re fully aware of the team we’re up against and the level.”.

Former Arsenal players Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Christian Norgaard could feature for Everton this afternoon.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two Iranian men were found guilty of spying on dissident journalists in Britain on behalf of Iran's Revolutionary Guard on Thursday.

British counterterrorism police mentioned the case reflected intensifying hostile Iranian activity in the country, an issue that recently made headlines amid the security scare at the RAF Fairford airbase that's a major operational site in Europe for the US Air Force.

The men, both in their 40s, were arrested last year, with Iran repeatedly rejecting the allegations against them.

The Woolwich Crown Court in London convicted one of the Iranian citizens not just of spying on journalists working for the Persian-language dissident TV channel Iran International, but of plotting a violent attack against one or more of them.

The second individual had also faced charges of plotting an attack but was only convicted of spying on the reporters.

One of the convicted defendants said he was acting under duress after his family was threatened, and the other said he did not know that his actions were assisting Iranian intelligence.

A third defendant, a 57-year-old Iranian man, was acquitted of all charges.

The men were accused of engaging in conduct likely to assist the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), Iran's multi-discipline military force that's seen as closer to the country's religious leadership and more influential than its regular armed forces.

The UK formally designated the IRGC as a threat to national security in July, meaning that supporting or assisting the organization can carry penalties of up to 14 years in prison as part of new rules on national security and state threats.

Sentencing in this case is still pending and is scheduled for mid-December.

"This was a calculated operation to spy on those critical of the Iranian regime," mentioned Frank Ferguson, chief prosecutor for the Crown Prosecution Service's special crime and counter-terrorism division.

The two men were accused of visiting addresses linked to their targets, taking photos and videos, and using platforms such as ChatGPT to research them online.

"Thankfully, the defendants were stopped before any attack could take place," prosecutor Ferguson mentioned.

Senior ‌National Coordinator for Counter Terrorism Policing Vicki Evans said that the IRGC or "middlemen" for Iranian intelligence were directing the plot.

Iran's government had repeatedly denied the allegations, with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi saying he was "disturbed" by the trio's arrests last May.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

There have been four cases targeting the Persian language television channel Iran International since late 2023.

In July, two Romanian men were jailed for stabbing a journalist outside his home in 2024.

A spokesman for the broadcaster's parent company, Volant Media, remarked in a statement that Thursday's verdicts "don't make the lives of our journalists any safer so long as the Islamic Republic of Iran continues its campaign of death threats and violence against them.".

Iran International reported that a British barrister was also one of the targets.

British law enforcement has been warning of an uptick of hostile Iranian activity in recent years, particularly since the US military operations against Tehran began earlier this year.

Most notably, the UK has accused Iran of being behind a suspected plot targeting the RAF Fairford base in September, after which US President Donald Trump withdrew some long-range bombers from the site.

Three men were indicted in the US in relation to that plot this week, while two others right now face charges in the UK.

But beyond this, the head of Britain's MI5 domestic intelligence agency Ken MacCullum said in October that Iran-linked operations had led to more than 50 arrests in the last year. He also said known cases of so-called state threats had more than quadrupled in a decade.

Counter-terrorism police chief Evans remarked she expected this trend to continue.

France this week also accused Iran of being behind a cyberattack targeting refrigeration units at hundreds of supermarkets in October, although Iran denied any involvement.

Sources indicate that european governments are on heightened alert for so-called hybrid warfare tactics, from Russia as well as Iran, amid the geopolitical tensions of recent years. New technologies like low-cost drones and AI are also threatening to make such activities cheaper, harder to trace, and potentially more effective.

Henry Pollock was at the centre of an East Midlands derby flare-up that sparked a second-half Leicester onslaught as Northampton were overpowered at a sodden Mattioli Woods Welford Road.

The England back row, never knowingly far from controversy, escalated a brawl at the end of the first half that Leicester prop Joe Heyes revealed “added fuel to the fire” of a Tigers side who roared impressively when they returned after the break.

The incident fired up a sell-out crowd and Leicester brought what had up to that point been a drab game to life with a storming second-half performance.

Three tries in a pulverising 13-minute spell overturned a half-time deficit and put the hosts on course for a bonus-point win over their arch-rivals that took them to second place in the Prem table.

Pollock, withdrawn after 52 minutes, may wish to reflect on the wisdom of riling the Tigers in their own lair.

“That was a proper Tigers second half and a really pleasing performance,” Geoff Parling, their director of rugby, noted.

“We got on the front foot and showed our power. The way the guys problem-solved was brilliant and I’m just really pleased with the emotional energy they threw into that game.

It’s a big day for Alex Coles, who celebrates his milestone 150th cap today.

The 27-year-old lock follows Fraser Dingwall, Rory Hutchinson and Alex Mitchell to become the fourth member of Saints’ current squad to reach 150 appearances for his boyhood club, eight years after making his debut in 2018.

Coles marks one of nine changes to Saints’ side for the Derby Day clash, with Emmanuel Iyogun, Curtis Langdon, Ed Prowse, Tom Pearson and Henry Pollock the other names coming into the forward pack.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of Leicester Tigers v Northampton Saints.

The Prem’s derby weekend continues today at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, where Geoff Parling’s side go head-to-head in with their East Midlands rivals.

Both Leicester and Northampton have two wins from the opening three rounds of the season and with both sides involved in a number of high-scoring encounters already in the upcoming campaign, we could be in for a real treat.

Tigers started the season with a 38-40 loss at home to Saracens, but bounced back promptly with wins over Gloucester and Newcastle Red Bulls. They will be itching to right a few wrongs after suffering a chastening Champions Cup defeat in Pau last week.

Northampton, meanwhile, have notched up wins over Newcastle Red Bulls and Bath either side of loss to Bristol Bears.

A win today for Saints would be their first on the road since defeating Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park in April.

“It (the East Midlands derby) means a lot to everyone, we know it will be a great atmosphere at Mattioli Woods Welford Road,” noted Parling.

“I don’t think with this sort of game either team has to build it up too much emotionally because that just comes, so I think it’s actually about being really really calm in the moment.”.

“Hopefully we can put the best of ourselves out there and I’m sure Saints will be able to do exactly the same.”.

Saints are without a victory in Leicester since January 2023, when a single point decided the 18-19 result.

Since then, the last five meetings between the sides have been won by the hosts on the day – with Saints last taking home the bragging rights when a Tom Litchfield hat-trick helped Northampton to a 45-31 win on home soil in last season’s league play-off.

Recent findings suggest that kick-off gets underway at 3.05pm. Stay with us here for all the latest updates.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 08:35 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 11:06 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Erling Haaland saw a first half equaliser controversially disallowed against Fulham, as Enzo Maresca's side only managed to fight back to earn a disappointing draw.
  • Haaland latched onto a beautifully bent cross from Iliman Ndiaye to bundle home from less than eight minutes after Rodrigo Muniz had given the visitors a shock lead at the Etihad.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By HARRY BAMFORTH, LIVE SPORTS COVERAGE REPORTER.

Published: 08:35 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 11:06 EST, 21 November 2026.

Erling Haaland saw a first half equaliser controversially disallowed against Fulham, as Enzo Maresca's side only managed to fight back to earn a disappointing draw.

Haaland latched onto a beautifully bent cross from Iliman Ndiaye to bundle home from less than eight minutes after Rodrigo Muniz had given the visitors a shock lead at the Etihad.

But despite Bernd Leno appearing to fumble the ball over the line and the referee's watch flashing to signify a goal, the man in the middle ruled the equaliser out for a foul on the Cottagers goalkeeper.

The decision has left both fans and pundits torn over whether the decision was harsh or whether it was the right call.

Former Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder Karen Carney noted her mind changed after having watched a replay of the incident.

Speaking on TNT Sports from the Etihad, she stated: 'My initial reaction was I thought the goalkeeper didn’t have control of it, and it should've been a goal, but then when you slow it down, (you can see it).

It has been revealed that erling Haaland has the ball in the back of the net, but it’s ruled out! ❌ 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/sKqY8Q7a9Z.

Erling Haaland has a first half equaliser for Man City chalked off against Fulham.

Sources indicate that 'People are going to shout at me through the TV. But I think the referee made the right decision.'.

Tottenham legend Glenn Hoddle, also on punditry duty in Manchester, felt the same.

He mentioned: 'I don’t know whether he had control of it, but I don’t think that comes into it. I think that’s the right decision, but it’s a very tough call. It could have gone either way.'.

The Premier League Match Centre clarified why the decision was made by Tom Bramall and the VAR team in Stockley Park.

A statement on social media read: 'The referee’s call of free-kick to Fulham and no goal to Manchester City was checked and confirmed by VAR – with the goalkeeper deemed to be in control of the ball.'.

They added that the VAR noted: 'The ball is in control between both hands and then is played out of that possession by the attacker, and then into the back of the net.'.

The laws of the game state that a goalkeeper is believed to be in control of the ball when the ball is 'between their hands/arms or between their hand(s)/arm(s) and any surface'.

It has been revealed that not all fans, of a Manchester City persuasion or not, felt that the right decision was made. Some believed that both Haaland and City should feel hard done by.

Haaland was left in disbelief by the referee's decision with many fans feeling the same.

Recent findings suggest that an Arsenal fan made their stance clear: 'Even as a rival, I honestly think this Haaland goal should’ve stood for Manchester City. Would’ve been p***** off if a Gyokeres goal like this for Arsenal was cancelled.'.

Recent findings suggest that A different fan added: 'Manchester City has been robbed. Haaland scored a clean goal here. The ball went in even before Haaland had contact with the keeper.

Not everyone agreed, though, with many X owners taking the opposite stance.

One noted: 'It’s explicitly a foul under the Laws. Don’t blame the ref if you don’t like the laws.'.

It has been revealed that another user wrote: 'I am also an Arsenal fan but the ball is still in two-palm contact. If you allow it, you will encourage outfield player challenging the save attempt And a foot to hand challenge will much more often lead to a broken wrist or thumb. That is an unfair advantage to outfield players.'.

City did go on to equalise in the second half, with Elliot Anderson bagging his first Premier League goal for the club by smashing home a sublime volley in the 57th minute.

Q: Just how frustrating was it last season?

It has been revealed that last season was tough. It was the first time I’d had a significant injury which kept setting me back. When you can’t find a solution to something, it’s frustrating.

Recent findings suggest that Q: I remember you breaking down against Liverpool and you looked broken. That must’ve been horrible to deal with?

Recent findings suggest that Q: What sort of approach did you take in your recovery? I imagine you tried several options.

I spoke to a few players who’ve had similar issues and reached out to someone in Germany – a specialist there – for a different approach to what I’d been doing, and the Club were on board with it.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hungary on Thursday noted it would ease abortion rules and ratify an international treaty on violence against women.
  • Under the planned changes to the so-called "heartbeat regulation," women will no longer be forced to listen to the vital signs of the fetus before an abortion.
  • Women will also be able to get emergency contraceptive pills without prescription.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hungary on Thursday noted it would ease abortion rules and ratify an international treaty on violence against women.

Under the planned changes to the so-called "heartbeat regulation," women will no longer be forced to listen to the vital signs of the fetus before an abortion.

Women will also be able to get emergency contraceptive pills without prescription.

The changes proposed by the upcoming government under Prime Minister Peter Magyar are a significant break with the conservative policies of his predecessor Viktor Orban.

The country also prepares to ratify the Istanbul Convention, a treaty aimed at preventing violence against women and domestic violence.

It has been revealed that hungarian law allows for most abortions to be performed up to 12 weeks, and up to 24 weeks in cases of severe developmental abnormalities. Until now, women were required to have a medical provider show them evidence of a definitive sign of fetal life, commonly understood as the so-called "fetal heartbeat," before deciding whether to have an abortion.

It has been revealed that the controversial 2022 policy had received widespread criticism from doctors and women’s rights groups as being cruel and humiliating. It will now be scrapped.

The policy had not led to a decline in abortions and according to Magyar, had raised "serious bioethical questions.".

The second major change is that emergency contraception will be available without prescription.

Further measures include changing the criminal code aimed at better protecting women, including making the misuse of intimate images a criminal offense and strengthening the treatment of victims of domestic violence during criminal proceedings.

According to recent reports, hungary also plans to ratify an international treaty on the protection of women which most other EU members have long ratified. The Istanbul Convention came into force in 2014 and, among other things, requires rape to be criminalized based on the absence of freely given consent.

"We are making it clear that sexual acts can only ⁠take ​place with the voluntary consent of the other party," ​Magyar said.

The government of his predecessor Orban had opposed the treaty, arguing that it promoted what it described as "gender ideology.".

"We are making a clear and accountable commitment to putting an end to the era of inaction," Magyar noted in a Facebook video.

Among the EU’s other members, only Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Lithuania and Slovakia have not yet ratified the convention.

The Istanbul Convention is a treaty by the Council of Europe, an international organization that promotes human rights and the rule of law across Europe and includes more countries than the member of the EU.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Amazon rainforest plays a key part in the cycling of carbon and water on regional and global scales, and is widely viewed as a perennially evergreen ecosystem. However, writing in Nature, Song et al.1 report that there are extended periods when trees in most of the rainforest remain leafless. Known as deciduousness, this state occurs between the shedding of old leaves and the emergence and early development (flushing) of fresh ones. The authors also found that hydroclimatic conditions such as annual rainfall have a more crucial role in determining this pattern of leaf behaviour than do soil properties and light availability. The seasonal variation in tropical leaf cover and photosynthetic activity in the Amazon observed by the authors is less pronounced than that seen for broadleaf trees in temperate and boreal climate zones.

Tech Report: What have the talks with Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi achieved for Ukraine?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The two-day talks between delegations from Ukraine, the US and Russia in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11 ended without a ceasefire agreement.
  • The main outcome was an agreement on a prisoner exchange.
  • It has been revealed that "We have agreed on the largest humanitarian release of prisoners, and tomorrow we will finalize the numbers," Jared Kushner announced after the talks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The two-day talks between delegations from Ukraine, the US and Russia in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11 ended without a ceasefire agreement.

The main outcome was an agreement on a prisoner exchange.

It has been revealed that "We have agreed on the largest humanitarian release of prisoners, and tomorrow we will finalize the numbers," Jared Kushner announced after the talks. US envoys Kushner and Steve Witkoff arrived in Moscow on Thursday, where they are due to meet President Vladimir Putin.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had earlier suggested an exchange of "1,000 for 1,000" prisoners, or "1,500 for 1,500." Russia noted a large-scale prisoner exchange with Ukraine could take place within the next two to three weeks.

Following the meetings, Zelenskyy wrote on Telegram that the parties had discussed security guarantees and that "the first step should be ending this war and ensuring Ukraine's security." He also stressed that Europe should be involved "at every stage of genuine diplomacy.".

Experts interviewed by DW agree that the main outcome of the talks is humanitarian.

"The agreement on a prisoner exchange is already a major step forward," indicates Artjom Bronzhukov of the Ukrainian think tank Polityka.

Pavlo Lakiychuk of the Ukrainian Center for Global Studies Strategy XXI also viewed it as a "very tangible result." He told DW that "getting our people back is already a major success. That is why it is worth continuing.".

A real breakthrough, he added, would be the release of civilian detainees from territories occupied since 2014, particularly people from Crimea, who have been held in Russian prisons for years.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Davyd Arakhamia, head of the ruling Servant of the People parliamentary faction and Ukraine's representative at the talks in Abu Dhabi, gave a positive assessment of the trilateral talks with the US and Russia, expressing hope that an agreement could be reached by the end of the year.

"I think the Russians came with extremely strict instructions, and it was difficult to ease the tone of the discussion. But the way the US representatives structured the talks with a view to the postwar situation in both countries opened up a dialogue, in my opinion, and allowed us to work together more productively," Arakhamia said at a joint press conference with US and Ukrainian representatives following the talks.

Iuliia Osmolovska of the Kyiv office of the international think tank GLOBSEC cautions against reading too much into the positive assessments of the talks from Washington and Kyiv.

"Diplomats taking part in negotiations will never say that everything went badly and that they have no expectations. Even when no results are achieved, they will still emphasize that the talks were constructive," she said. "For anyone familiar with diplomatic language, these are simply standard phrases.".

Osmolovska points to a joint assessment by 71 Ukrainian security and defense experts published by GLOBSEC in the summer. According to the assessment, the chances of a peace agreement or at least a ceasefire being reached this year or next stand at just 19%.

It has been revealed that she blames this on the fact that neither side is "ready" for genuine negotiations. Russia, in particular, has yet to accept that its objectives cannot be achieved by military means. "What we are seeing now is more of a farce, an attempt by all sides to put a brave face on things and create the impression that something is moving forward," Osmolovska mentioned.

Artjom Bronzhukov sees the talks as a way for Moscow to buy time.

"The visits by the Russian delegation, particularly under the leadership of Vladimir Medinsky, are nothing more than an attempt to stall and sell empty promises to the US administration in the form of grand agreements, in order to continue receiving so-called gestures of goodwill from Washington, such as the lifting of sanctions on Russian diesel," the political scientist states.

Sources indicate that ahead of the talks, several Western media outlets reported on upcoming US proposals concerning disputed territories. The Economist, for example, reported on a proposal to redraw the administrative boundaries of the Donetsk and Luhansk regions. However, a member of the Ukrainian delegation stressed that there had "never been any discussion of concessions on territories occupied by Russia.".

Washington made no official comment on the reports.

Kyrylo Budanov, a member of the negotiating delegation and head of the Ukrainian president's office, declined to say whether Russia had used the talks to demand that Ukrainian troops withdraw from the Donbas. Asked by journalists whether Moscow was still insisting that Ukraine pull out of the region, Budanov stated the content of the negotiations would remain confidential until an agreement was reached.

"The issues discussed in the talks are matters for negotiation. The only thing that matters is the outcome. Once we achieve it, it will be made public," Budanov remarked.

The head of the Russian delegation, Vladimir Medinsky, took a different tone, declaring that "every inch of our land will be returned to Russia one way or another." He was responding to reports in European media that Ukraine was rejecting territorial concessions.

In addition to the Crimean Peninsula, annexed in 2014, Russian President Vladimir Putin claims the four Ukrainian regions of Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson in their entirety as Russian territory, even though Russia does not have full military control over them.

"Putin is not fighting over villages and ruined cowsheds in the Donbas. He is fighting for geopolitical influence and trying to exploit the collapse of the old world order," states Artjom Bronzhukov.

Recent findings suggest that the expert from the Polityka think tank recalls that Ukraine was already asked in early 2026 to withdraw its troops from the part of the Donbas it controls and turn the area into a free economic zone. Such a zone "would very quickly become a Russian-controlled area," he warns.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Pavlo Lakiychuk questions the idea of changing administrative boundaries.

"Why would Putin stop there?" asks the expert from the Strategy XXI center. In his view, US negotiators are seeking to extract unilateral concessions from Ukraine "step by step" without demanding anything in return from Russia.

It has been revealed that iuliia Osmolovska describes the proposal as "very original," but says it would pose risks for Ukraine's leadership. Even if the Ukrainian delegation agreed to it, which Osmolovska doubts, the decision would have to be explained to the public, which, she says, is not ready to accept it.

The GLOBSEC expert points out that, following the last harsh winter, marked by shortages of electricity and heating, only 5% of Ukrainians were willing to make concessions to Russia in exchange for an end to attacks on the energy sector.

Following the meeting between Jared Kushner, US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Vladimir Putin in Moscow, Volodymyr Zelenskyy mentioned he wants to "coordinate positions with the Americans once again." No further trilateral meetings have been announced so far.

Sources indicate that iuliia Osmolovska believes the parties will sooner or later have to admit that the negotiations have reached a dead end. She expects each side to return to military action.

Industry observers note that pavlo Lakiychuk, by contrast, believes the talks should continue, if only to secure the return of prisoners. He is also convinced that Europeans "will always be there," because the issue is not just the Russian-Ukrainian war but the security of the entire continent.

This article was originally published in Ukrainian.

What Martin O’Neill wouldn’t give to see more of this until the point where the cavalry appears on top of the hill in January.

Celtic wins with bells and whistles attached have been as rare as hen’s teeth since this campaign began.

That the supporters witnessed one in trying circumstances felt significant given the arduous schedule which awaits in the coming six weeks.

In a recent development, despite having no option but to piece together a midfield, O’Neill watched his side create a slew of opportunities. They took four with as many different scorers and might well have had more.

Recent findings suggest that A display brimming with enterprise and imagination boded well for what lies ahead. For the first time since September, Celtic have chalked up three straight wins. Ahead of the trip to face Torreense in Portugal on Thursday, it appears that a bit of wind is back in the sails.

In a recent development, this was as comprehensive a win as the scoreline suggests. The champions were never in danger from the moment Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain edged them in front just after the half hour mark.

Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain celebrates Celtic's first goal against St Mirren.

According to recent reports, in danger of becoming something of a forgotten man, the former England man rolled back the years here with a display which reminded you why he once wore the shirts of Liverpool and Arsenal. On this evidence, he still has a contribution to make at Parkhead.

The outcome was more or less settled by the interval. Camilo Duran continued his outstanding first season in Glasgow’s East End with another assured finish.

Luke McCowan, a man who’s not exactly had his critics to seek in recent times, netted the third before the break, his goal a just reward for a tidy afternoon’s work.

On a day when O’Neill would have had concerns about his midfield, Callum McGregor also netted with a crisp strike from the edge of the box.

St Mirren’s consolation, coming from Killian Phillips’ penalty, was too little too late.

On Friday, Buddies boss Craig McLeish had made some salient points about the self-interest which is holding back Scottish football.

Recent findings suggest that it’s hard not to like McLeish’s attitude and the style of football his side are playing. But they are continuing to lose goals far too easily. They could find themselves getting dragged into trouble if they don’t swiftly address it.

Celtic's Camilo Duran celebrates after scoring their second goal in the 4-1 win.

On Friday, O’Neill had rejected the suggestion that Haissem Hassan had been omitted from the squad which faced Kilmarnock because he needed a kick up the backside. Yet, curiously, there was no sign of the Egyptian again here.

With Benjamin Nygren and Mika Baur injured, O’Neill hoped that a combination of McGregor, McCowan and Oxlade-Chamberlain would have enough.

Kasper Hogh’s chances of ending a run of 16 games without a goal weren’t helped by him starting on the bench. He didn’t leave it.

With just one win in nine coming into this, Craig McLeish’s side were short on points yet they were not short on confidence.

Although they played some stuff which was very easy on the eye, an inability to keep the ball out of the net cost them dear again.

Recent findings suggest that mcCowan had an early shot blocked before Colby Donovan had a weak effort saved. McCowan also hesitated to take a first-time strike with Louis Jackson doing enough to protect Jacob Chapman’s goal.

Celtic actually had the ball in the net twice before they made it count. Duran planted a header and a shot in the visitors’ net only to discover that the offside flag had been raised.

Jota sparked a sweeping move which saw Yang Hyun-jun tee up McCowan. Paul Nsio became the latest Saints player to frustrate the Celtic midfielder with a block.

Recent findings suggest that saints were aggrieved that Yang won a free-kick by going to ground too easily just before the opener. They may have had a point. That didn’t excuse the defending which followed.

Cameron Carter-Vickers rolled the ball in Yang’s direction. The winger burst away from Declan John and assessed his options.

His cut-back for the unmarked Oxlade-Chamberlain was inch-perfect. The former England midfielder swept home his first goal since netting against the same opponent in April.

Saints might well have levelled immediately. Ismeal Kabia wriggled away from Donovan and picked out Eseosa Sule. Liam Scales did well to prevent the forward netting from seven yards.

Recent findings suggest that celtic then cut through Saints with embarrassing ease. A straight pass sent Yang clear on goal. He should have gone for glory, but instead tried to square the ball to allow Duran a tap-in. Alex Gogic had other ideas and knocked the ball away for a corner.

Celtic midfielder Luke McCowan and St Mirren's Paul Nsio battle for the ball.

McLeish’s hopes of making it to the break still in the contest unravelled in the final five minutes of the first period.

It has been revealed that kieran Tierney’s decision to swap flanks paid dividends with a brilliant in-swinging cross. Duran ghosted onto it and cushioned the ball beyond Chapman with his left foot to claim his 14th goal of his debut season.

Jota might well have made it three-nil seconds later and he fired Oxlade-Chamberlain’s lay-off straight at the keeper.

There was no hope for Chapman as Celtic all but wrapped up the win three minutes before the interval.

It has been revealed that tierney was again the provider, his energy taking him to the line and allowing him to cross. McCowan calmly stroked home his second goal of the season.

Industry observers note that saints kept going seeking a goal which might have made it interesting. Kabia’s strike forced Sam Johnstone into a smart stop down to his right.

Industry observers note that yang ought to have killed the contest but blazed over while leaning back. Skipper McGregor showed him how to do it as he buried a right foot shot low in the bottom left-hand corner from the edge of the box after a defender had taken the ball off Duran’s toe.

Saints did get on the board thanks to Phillips’ penalty conversion, the award coming after Johnstone clattered Calvin Ramsay as he punched clear.

In a recent development, O’Neill was still able to send on Shim Mheaka and James Forrest with Austin Trusty returning to warm applause. Joel van den Berg had already been introduced for his debut along with Callum Osmand. The Dutch teenager indicated up well.

#105967. Can the EU make it harder to trick consumers online?

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (806 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Can the EU make it harder to trick consumers online?

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (806 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Under the European Commission's proposed Digital Fairness Act (DFA), a organization would have to remind you before the free trial ends and get your explicit agreement before it can start charging you.
  • The Commission presented the proposal on Wednesday.
  • "We haven't seen that kind of reform in consumer protection in the last 20 years," Agustin Reyna, director general of the European Consumer Organisation (BEUC), told DW.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Under the European Commission's proposed Digital Fairness Act (DFA), a organization would have to remind you before the free trial ends and get your explicit agreement before it can start charging you. The proposed law would also make it easier to cancel a subscription online and require reminders before certain contracts renew automatically.

The Commission presented the proposal on Wednesday. It wants to give consumers more control over how much time and money they spend online.

"We haven't seen that kind of reform in consumer protection in the last 20 years," Agustin Reyna, director general of the European Consumer Organisation (BEUC), told DW.

Sources indicate that his organization pushed for stronger EU rules against manipulative online practices. He sees the proposal as a good starting point for tackling problems that frustrate consumers every day.

The proposal also includes a ban on manipulative marketing tactics, so-called "dark patterns." A concrete example: You are trying to reserve a hotel room and the website claims that only three are left, a potentially false claim to pressure you into buying.

A concert ticket that gets more expensive while you're waiting in an online queue raises a different problem. The price could still go up in the process, but the seller would have to show the current price while you wait and tell you the maximum you could be asked to pay.

Online games that encourage users to spend their money to advance are also targeted. Children would no longer be able to pay to win or get to the next level of their online game.

Marketing and personalized ads would need to be clearly marked and restricted in the case of children. Consumers should get the option to switch off doomscrolling functions such as the autoplay of videos, showing one clip after the other. With these new rules, the EU wants to make apps and websites less addictive.

In a recent development, for Christoph Busch, an academic with a focus on consumer law and digital services based at Osnabrück University in Germany, the option to opt out doesn't go far enough. He argues that a version in which consumers actively have to choose to opt into those functions would be more effective.

In a recent development, "But then there is always the question of proportionality," Busch mentioned. "And I think here the European legislators are trying to balance different interests.".

These competing interests are particularly visible in the gaming industry, where interest groups have warned that the proposed EU restrictions could hurt developers and leave players with fewer options to choose from.

Video Games Europe and the European Games Developer Federation called the proposal "unworkable, unjustified and disproportionate," arguing that a ban on selling children features that help them win or advance is worded so broadly that it "could cover almost any purchase in a game.".

For Busch, this argument doesn't hold. "If your business model is based on addictive design features, then maybe your business model has to be reviewed," he said.

Catalina Goanta, an associate professor of private law and technology at Utrecht University, emphasized in an interview with DW that "regulation can very easily slide into overregulation.".

Recent findings suggest that even though she believes that the DFA is a solid and reasonable compromise, she argues that prohibiting dark patterns and doomscrolling altogether would be too prohibitive. Many of the complications consumers right now face could be resolved by enforcing existing regulation more effectively, she noted.

She points to the fact that the EU has made a name for itself in the past by adding newly introduced rules and regulations that have made it more difficult to access the European market, especially for small online businesses.

BEUC director Agustin Reyna disagrees.

"Instead of having 27 different regulations to adhere to, companies will now only get one," Reyna said.

For him, this speaks for simplification, especially when the responsibility for compliance is shared between online influencers and the platforms they publish on.

According to the new legislation, the EU would have the possibility to impose fines of up to six percent of a manufacturer's global annual revenue should the company violate the law.

The European Parliament and the Council, which represents member state governments, still have to agree on the text and formally adopt it. All experts agree that in that process, changes are still very likely.

"It will be a difficult trialogue, especially in this climate of simplification and deregulation with a focus on strengthening European competitiveness," said Christoph Busch. In that climate, it is not easy to add consumer rights, he adds.

According to recent reports, agustin Reyna is more optimistic. "The parliament is a divided house, much more than in the past," he notes. "But consumer protection is a subject that brings parties together because it brings tangible outcomes to people.".

This was hardly “the Battle of the Bridge”, but Chelsea blew up during a ridiculous 10-minute spell towards the end of a game in which Tottenham had bossed possession but not looked like scoring.

"It's PETULANT from Cole Palmer...you have to take it on the chin" Jamie Redknapp and Daniel Sturridge react to Cole Palmer's pair of yellow cards 🟥 https://t.co/Voxoo3Ea7V.

Palmer was just about the only Chelsea player not to have been sent off last season, but it seems that Alonso has not yet managed to deal with the club’s disciplinary problem.

Jordan Henderson had given Palmer a talking to at the end of the win at Everton in which the forward was booked. But he evidently did not heed the advice or the words of his manager.

Alonso had noted he was confident his players could keep calm ahead of the game, but he got that wrong – along with his team selection and substitutions.

Meet ‘egoviruses’: the surprise microbes living in the guts of millions of people

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (733 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Many giant viruses can be seen under a light microscope.Credit: Gabrielle Voinot/Eurelios/Look at Sciences/SPL.
  • Roughly 180 million people could be carrying previously unknown giant viruses inside their guts.
  • Large and giant viruses in the phylum Nucleocytoviricota are a vast group of DNA viruses — some are so substantial that they can be seen under a light microscope — that mostly infect single-celled organisms in the environment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Many giant viruses can be seen under a light microscope.Credit: Gabrielle Voinot/Eurelios/Look at Sciences/SPL.

Roughly 180 million people could be carrying previously unknown giant viruses inside their guts. Microbiologists say that these ‘egoviruses’ could be the missing link between giant viruses that infect single-celled organisms and distantly related poxviruses, such as those that cause smallpox and mpox, which can infect people and animals directly. The findings are published in Nature1.

Large and giant viruses in the phylum Nucleocytoviricota are a vast group of DNA viruses — some are so substantial that they can be seen under a light microscope — that mostly infect single-celled organisms in the environment.

Poxviruses are an outlier in the giant-virus world because they can directly infect humans and animals and their origin is a mystery, claims Fasséli Coulibaly, a structural biologist at Monash University in Melbourne, Australia. Egoviruses could be the evolutionary bridge between microorganism-infecting giant viruses called asfuviruses and pathogenic poxviruses, he says.

Tom Delmont, a microbial ecologist at the French National Centre for Scientific Research in Paris, and his colleagues discovered egoviruses while combing through online libraries of metagenomes. These contain the genetic information of all the organisms in a particular environment, which means that researchers can hunt for microbes without having to cultivate them. When the team scanned for a single gene found in most nucleocytoviruses, they discovered egoviruses — the only type of nucleocytovirus that is prevalent in the gut.

Industry observers note that they found egovirus DNA in gut samples from people, buffalo, goats, chickens, deer and pigs. Six clades were unique to people. One of these clades is estimated to be present in roughly 1% of the global population, on the basis of the presence of at least one of two egovirus proteins in the samples they analysed.

The researchers detected these proteins in samples spanning a large proportion of the human population, from the Hadza, a hunter-gatherer group in Tanzania, to populations in Europe, the United States and South America, indicates Delmont. That suggests that egoviruses have been inhabiting the human gut for a long time, he adds.

That egoviruses are found in many animal species, including people, and are widespread around the world highlights that giant viruses are more diverse than previously thought, says Subir Sarker, a molecular virologist at James Cook University in Townsville, Queensland. “This is a really groundbreaking study,” he adds.

Industry observers note that to identify potential hosts for egoviruses in the gut, the team compared the amount of genetic overlap between egoviruses and organisms with a nucleus. The researchers found the most overlap with single-celled organisms that help ruminants, such as cows, to digest their food.

Phelan then made two further changes on 68 minutes as Ruby Mace and Hikaru Kitagawa replaced Clare Wheeler and Vignola.

With eight minutes remaining, Naomi Layzell – who claimed the Player of the Match award when the two sides met in the WSL – came on in place of Aurora Galli.

Despite a late push for an equaliser, United stood firm and succumbed the Toffees to their first defeat in the Subway Players Cup.

  • When asked by DW during the European Political Community summit in Dublin why Europe should only get one seat at the table while the US gets two, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas responded with a wry, ironic laugh ― clearly a sign of the frustration felt by European leaders about being sidelined thus far.
  • The summit of 47 European leaders in Dublin comes in the wake of a diplomatic tour by two Donald Trump administration advisers, the president's son-in-law Jared Kushner and special envoy Steve Witkoff, to talks in Abu Dhabi, followed by a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

European leaders are under pressure to put forward a name to represent them in Ukraine peace talks after US envoy Steve Witkoff told reporters that the Europeans will be present at the next meetings.

When asked by DW during the European Political Community summit in Dublin why Europe should only get one seat at the table while the US gets two, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas responded with a wry, ironic laugh ― clearly a sign of the frustration felt by European leaders about being sidelined thus far.

The summit of 47 European leaders in Dublin comes in the wake of a diplomatic tour by two Donald Trump administration advisers, the president's son-in-law Jared Kushner and special envoy Steve Witkoff, to talks in Abu Dhabi, followed by a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow.

The pair then hot-footed their way to Dublin to debrief Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelekenskyy.

Zelenskyy and Kushner also said Thursday that Europeans would be at the table for the next talks with Russia on ending the war.

According to recent reports, kallas is one of the figures tipped as most likely to represent the EU in any future talks to end Russia's war against Ukraine, alongside EU Council President Antonio Costa. As yet, the EU hasn’t been able to land on one central figure to send ― many of the national leaders want to be present themselves.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz insisted Europe will be present.

"At the table must be sitting Ukraine, must be sitting the Europeans, must be sitting the Americans, and naturally Russia," he told reporters in Dublin.

But he, like many other leaders, played down the idea of appointing a special envoy for the talks.

Zelenskyy is insistent on European involvement in the peace talks.

"Not directly yet, and not yet when the Russians are at the table," he told the other leaders during the Dublin meetings. "But Europeans are already involved. And we need to make sure that Europe becomes a regular part of these negotiations.".

Industry observers note that europe’s division over exactly who should be present has caused a public battle to erupt. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni wrote an excoriating letter to Costa last week, bemoaning the lack of unity.

"By projecting the image of a Europe that is in disarray, we are merely serving the interests of those who want this war to continue," wrote Meloni.

European leaders had even seemed divided over their level of frustration about the situation.

Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Jansa remarked in Dublin that it was creating a "bad mood" among leaders, however Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs disputed those comments saying, "I don’t feel that.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The palpable fear among the leaders in Dublin is that the US will accept Russia's demands that Europe changes the way it structures its own security, mainly through the NATO military alliance, in exchange for a seat at the table.

Putin remarked a commitment that Ukraine will never join NATO and even the potential rolling back of the alliance to remove newly introduced joiners Finland and Sweden, could be among his demands.

Sources indicate that "What do we hear from them [Europeans]?" asked Putin during the meeting with Kushner and Witkoff in Moscow. "That once a peace agreement is signed, they will immediately deploy troops in Ukraine. This is a legitimate target for us, so the war will resume immediately.".

This is exactly the kind of rhetoric the European leaders say they are most wary of, especially those in Russia’s direct neighborhood.

"Right now, we are in the [Russian] trap," stated Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal. "If something is a threat to you, will you discuss your defense with the threat [itself]?".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

US President Donald Trump stated publicly that he was hoping for a "very massive, beautiful agreement" that "might involve all of Europe.".

Zelensky remarked he found the US approach "a bit strange.".

Many of Europe's leaders speaking in Dublin referenced previous agreements with Russia that they believe Moscow has breached.

They include the 1975 Helsinki Accords, the 1990 Paris Charter, 1997 NATO-Russia Founding Act and the one they consider most crucial: the 1994 Budapest Memorandum, which forbids Russia from using force against Ukraine unless in self-defense.

The rancor over the seat at the peace talks is drawing focus away from arguably the bigger battle in the EU now ― how to fund Ukraine as the war continues.

Back in October, the European Commission identified a €70 billion hole in the EU’s funding it had promised for Ukraine’s economy.

Slovakia’s Prime Minister Robert Fico has opposed any further financial and military support for Ukraine.

But Germany's Merz warned he could block the EU's next seven-year budget unless member states agree to contribute to Ukraine's financing.
